findings.title: readSequence loop mishandles indefinite length and can loop forever
findings.body: readLength() returns -1 for indefinite-length encoding, so the `while (length > 0)` loop is skipped and an empty list is returned without any error. Separately, if readNext() returns a zero-length array, `length` never decreases and the loop does not terminate. Truncated or malformed signatures are therefore not rejected cleanly.

findings.title: Incorrect length bound check
findings.body: The out-of-bounds check is only done for long-form lengths, and the comparison `length >= limit` is against the whole input rather than the remaining bytes. Short-form lengths are never checked. The subsequent `new byte[length]` in read() can therefore be sized by malformed input, with failure only at EOF. Inside nested decoders, `limit` is the size of the sub-array, which makes the check inconsistent.

findings.title: Dead code: redundant ASN1 encodings
findings.body: The two `ASN1Encoder.create().write(...)` calls at lines 114-115 discard their results and do nothing. They are leftovers and should be removed.

findings.title: getBouncyCastleProvider returns the default KeyStore's provider
findings.body: The method returns the provider of the default KeyStore type, which is SUN, not BouncyCastle. Callers that use `BouncyIntegration.PROVIDER` can end up with a mismatched provider name. This is misleading and is likely to break when other CryptoProvider methods are invoked in the authz-client.

findings.title: New abstract method breaks existing CryptoProvider implementations
findings.body: `order()` is added as an abstract interface method without a default. Any third-party or other-module CryptoProvider implementation will fail to compile. Providing `default int order() { return 0; }` would avoid the break.

findings.title: Ties between providers resolved silently and nondeterministically
findings.body: The check that rejected multiple providers was removed. Providers with equal order (e.g. Default, Elytron and FIPS are all 200) are now chosen by ServiceLoader order, so a misconfigured classpath no longer fails fast. The ignored providers are logged only at debug level.
